A_target.statement:
Let $G = \gen {S \mid R}$ be a [[Definition:Group Presentation|group presentation]].
Let $H$ be a [[Definition:Group|group]] generated by elements indexed by $S$ in which every relator of $R$ holds.
Then $H$ is a [[Definition:Quotient Group|quotient]] of $G$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\phi: G \to H$ be a [[Definition:Group Homomorphism|homomorphism]] and $N$ a [[Definition:Normal Subgroup|normal subgroup]] of $G$ with $N \subseteq \map \ker \phi$.
Then $\phi$ factors uniquely through $G / N$.

substitutions.the ambient object: the free group F on the generating set S
substitutions.the normal subgroup being collapsed: the normal closure of the relator set R

derived.the factorization of any compatible map: any group generated by S in which the relators vanish receives a surjection from F/N
derived.the universality of the quotient: F/N is the largest such group

validity_conditions: Any set map from a free basis extends uniquely to a homomorphism, so a choice of generators gives a surjection from F onto the target group.
The kernel of that surjection is normal and contains R, hence contains the normal closure of R.
The universal property then factors the surjection through F/N, exhibiting the target as a quotient of the presented group.
proof_plan: Let $F$ be the [[Definition:Free Group|free group]] on $S$ and $N$ the [[Definition:Normal Closure|normal closure]] of $R$ in $F$, so $G = F / N$.

By the [[Universal Property of Free Group|universal property]] of $F$, the assignment of generators extends to a homomorphism $\phi: F \to H$, which is [[Definition:Surjection|surjective]] as the images generate $H$.

Each relator lies in $\map \ker \phi$.
As $\map \ker \phi$ is normal and $N$ is the smallest normal subgroup containing $R$:
:$N \subseteq \map \ker \phi$
